questions.text: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below it:
questions.passage: Yoga is the ancient system to keep a person fit in body and mind. It is basically a system of self-treatment. According to the yogic view, diseases, disorders and ailments are the result of some faulty way of living, bad habits, lack of proper knowledge and unsuitable food. The diseases are thus the resultant state of a short or prolonged malfunctioning of the body system. Since the root cause of a disease lies in the mistakes of the individual himself. The yoga expert shows only the path and works no more than a counsellor. The yogic practice of treatment comprises three steps namely diet, proper yogic practice and proper knowledge of things about the self.

parts.statement: The root cause of disease lies in ____.
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (b)

Explanation:
According to the passage, 'the root cause of a disease lies in the mistakes of the individual himself.' Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

parts.statement: The word 'prolonged' means:
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (b)

Explanation:
The word 'prolonged' refers to something continuing for a long duration of time. Among the given choices, 'Very old' is the closest suitable meaning.

parts.statement: The main causes of diseases and disorders are:
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (d)

Explanation:
The passage explicitly mentions that diseases result from a faulty way of living, bad habits, lack of knowledge, and unsuitable food. Thus, 'All of the above' is correct.

parts.statement: Yoga is the ancient system to keep a person ____.
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (c)

Explanation:
The opening line of the passage states: 'Yoga is the ancient system to keep a person fit in body and mind.'

parts.statement: The Yogic practice of treatment does not comprise ____.

options.text: proper knowledge of things about the self
proper knowledge of things about others

parts.correct_answer: proper knowledge of things about others
parts.explanation:

Explanation:
The three steps mentioned in the passage are diet, proper yogic practice, and proper knowledge of things about the self. Knowledge about others is not included.

questions.text: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below:
questions.passage: An American enlisted himself in the Spanish army. He did not know the Spanish language. The Commander informed that the King would come on inspection after six months. The King usually asked three questions: 'What is your age?', 'Since when have you been in the army?', and 'Are you satisfied with your lodging and boarding?' The Commander taught him the answers and he crammed them. As usual the King came on inspection. Looking at the new soldier, he asked, 'Since when have you been in my army?' 'Sir, 25 years' replied the soldier. The King was taken aback. He asked him the second question, 'Then what is your age?' 'Six months', the soldier humbly replied. 'Am I mad or you?' the King asked irritatingly. 'Sir, both' was the quick answer.

parts.statement: The Soldier did not know ____ language.
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (b)

Explanation:
The passage explicitly mentions: 'He did not know the Spanish language.'

parts.statement: The King would come on inspection ____.
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (b)

Explanation:
The Commander informed the soldier that 'the King would come on inspection after six months.'

parts.statement: Who taught the answers to the soldier?
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (d)

Explanation:
According to the passage, 'The Commander taught him the answers and he crammed them.'

parts.statement: What is the actual age of the soldier?
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (c)

Explanation:
The soldier mixed up the order of the memorized answers. His actual age was 25 years, whereas six months was his duration of service in the army.

parts.statement: A word from the passage which means check/survey:
parts.explanation:
Correct Option: (c)

Explanation:
The word 'inspection' refers to an official examination, check, or survey.

questions.text: Read the passage carefully and answer the questions given below it:
questions.passage: Man is made up of many qualities, both good and bad, and among the latter is anger. The nature of every human being is such that anything that gives offence to his sentiments or goes against his principles, excites his anger. The evils which result from anger are many. Under its influence, a man loses his power of reasoning and judgement. Not being able to retain control over himself when angry, he does not know what he is doing or saying. Under its influence, a man puts off his balance to the extent that he forgets his duty towards his superiors and may even say things which are extremely insulting to them.

essay_topics.name: Give a suitable title to the passage.
essay_topics.answer: The Evils of Anger / Harmful Effects of Anger

essay_topics.name: Make notes of the above passage.
essay_topics.answer:
TITLE: The Evils of Anger

NOTES:
1. Nature of Man:
   1.1 Possesses both good and bad qualities.
   1.2 Anger is a prominent bad quality.

2. Causes of Anger:
   2.1 Offence to sentiments.
   2.2 Actions going against personal principles.

3. Evils/Effects of Anger:
   3.1 Loss of power of reasoning and judgment.
   3.2 Loss of self-control.
   3.3 Unawareness of words and actions.
   3.4 Forgetting duties toward superiors.
   3.5 Using insulting language.

parts.statement: You are Anmol, residing at 50, Krishnapuram Colony, Shivpuri. Write a letter to your friend telling him about your Hostel Life.

Shivpuri (M.P.)

I hope this letter finds you in good health and high spirits. I am writing to share my experience of my new hostel life with you.

next_question.text: Write an essay on any ONE of the following topics in about 150 words:

parts.statement: Science: Curse or Boon
parts.explanation:
SCIENCE: CURSE OR BOON

Introduction:
We live in an era of science and technology. Science has fundamentally transformed human life, making it far more comfortable, convenient, and efficient.

Science as a Boon:
Science has provided us with extraordinary inventions such as electricity, computers, smartphones, and high-speed transportation. In the field of medicine, advanced diagnostic techniques and drugs have eradicated deadly diseases and extended human life expectancy. Modern communication has brought the world together as a global village.

Science as a Curse:
However, science becomes a curse when misused. The invention of lethal weapons of mass destruction, such as nuclear bombs, poses a constant threat to humanity. Uncontrolled industrialization has also led to severe environmental pollution, global warming, and ecological imbalance.

Conclusion:
Science itself is neutral; its impact depends entirely on how human beings choose to utilize it. Used for human welfare, it is a magnificent boon; misused for destruction, it becomes a curse.

parts.statement: Importance of Trees
parts.explanation:
IMPORTANCE OF TREES

Introduction:
Trees are among the most valuable natural resources on Earth. They are essential for the survival and sustenance of all living organisms.

Benefits of Trees:
Trees release life-giving oxygen through photosynthesis and absorb harmful carbon dioxide, thereby maintaining the atmospheric balance and mitigating global warming. They supply us with food, fruits, timber, shade, and medicinal herbs. Furthermore, trees bind the soil to prevent erosion, help regulate rainfall patterns, and provide shelter to wildlife.

Need for Protection:
Due to rapid urbanization and deforestation, the number of trees is declining drastically, leading to severe environmental crises. Planting more trees (afforestation) is crucial to restore ecological balance.

Conclusion:
Trees are the lungs of our planet. Protecting trees is vital for ensuring a healthy and sustainable future for mankind.

parts.statement: Electric Vehicles
parts.explanation:
ELECTRIC VEHICLES

Introduction:
Electric Vehicles (EVs) are emerging as a major technological alternative in the automotive industry. They run on electric motors powered by rechargeable battery packs rather than conventional fossil fuels.

Advantages:
The primary benefit of EVs is that they produce zero direct tailpipe emissions, thereby significantly reducing urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, they are economically efficient over time due to lower fuel and maintenance costs.

Challenges:
Despite their advantages, EVs currently face hurdles such as high initial purchasing costs, limited charging infrastructure, and long battery charging durations.

Conclusion:
Electric vehicles represent the future of sustainable transportation. With government incentives and rapid technological advancements, EVs will play a pivotal role in creating a cleaner environment.

parts.statement: Any Historical Building
parts.explanation:
A HISTORICAL BUILDING: THE TAJ MAHAL

Introduction:
India possesses a rich historical and cultural heritage. Among its numerous magnificent monuments, the Taj Mahal in Agra stands out as a world-famous architectural masterpiece.

History and Architecture:
The Taj Mahal was constructed by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife, Mumtaz Mahal. Built entirely of pure white marble on the banks of the River Yamuna, it took nearly 22 years to complete. It is renowned for its symmetrical design, beautiful domes, and intricate marble carvings.

Global Recognition:
Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the Seven Wonders of the World, it attracts millions of domestic and international tourists every year.

Conclusion:
The Taj Mahal stands as a timeless symbol of love and a monumental testimony to India's glorious historical craftsmanship.

parts.statement: Problem of Pollution
parts.explanation:
THE PROBLEM OF POLLUTION

Introduction:
Pollution has become one of the most pressing challenges of the modern world. It refers to the contamination of the natural environment by harmful physical or chemical substances.

Types and Causes:
Pollution exists in various forms—Air, Water, Soil, and Noise pollution. Uncontrolled industrial emissions, vehicular exhaust, deforestation, and improper waste disposal are the primary drivers of pollution. It leads to severe respiratory illnesses, climate change, and habitat destruction.

Solutions:
To combat pollution, we must switch to renewable energy sources, enforce strict industrial emission standards, minimize plastic usage, and promote large-scale afforestation.

Conclusion:
Pollution poses a grave threat to the planet. Collective efforts by citizens, industries, and governments are imperative to preserve a clean environment for future generations.

parts.statement: Write a paragraph in about 150 words on 'A friend in need is a friend indeed'.
parts.explanation:
A FRIEND IN NEED IS A FRIEND INDEED

The proverb 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' highlights the true essence and test of genuine friendship. Human beings naturally seek companions to share their joy and experiences. However, fair-weather friends remain close only during times of prosperity and happiness, drifting away when adversity strikes. In contrast, a true friend stands firmly by our side during moments of hardship, distress, and crisis. Such a friend offers unconditional emotional support, selfless help, and honest counsel without expecting anything in return. True friendship is built on the pillars of mutual trust, honesty, and empathy. Difficult times act as a mirror that separates insincere companions from genuine ones. In conclusion, true friendship is a priceless gift that is proven during adversity. We should cherish real friends and strive to be equally dependable companions to others.

parts.statement: He found {BLANK} one-rupee note.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: a

Explanation:
Although the word 'one' begins with the vowel 'o', it produces a consonant sound ('w' sound). Hence, the indefinite article 'a' is used.

parts.statement: There is {BLANK} hope of his recovery.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: a little

Explanation:
'Hope' is an uncountable noun. Therefore, 'a little' is the correct determiner, whereas 'a few' and 'many' are used with countable nouns.

parts.statement: It {BLANK} rain today.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: may

Explanation:
The modal verb 'may' is used to express factual possibility or likelihood, such as in weather predictions.

parts.statement: Walk carefully {BLANK} you would fall.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: otherwise

Explanation:
'Otherwise' is a conjunction used to indicate the negative consequence that will follow if the advice is not followed.

parts.statement: {BLANK} there is a will, there is a way.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: Where

Explanation:
This is a standard well-known English proverb: 'Where there is a will, there is a way.'

parts.statement: Listen {BLANK} me carefully.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: to

Explanation:
The verb 'listen' is conventionally followed by the preposition 'to' when taking an object.

parts.statement: I {BLANK} my friend yesterday.
parts.explanation:
Correct Answer: met

Explanation:
The time expression 'yesterday' indicates a completed action in the simple past tense, requiring the second form of the verb 'met'.

parts.statement: Ravi did his work. (Change into negative)
parts.explanation:
Negative Sentence: Ravi did not do his work.

Explanation:
In the simple past tense, negative sentences are formed using the auxiliary 'did not' followed by the base form of the verb ('do').

parts.statement: My grandfather is too old to walk. (Rewrite the sentence using 'so...that')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: My grandfather is so old that he cannot walk.

Explanation:
The 'too...to' structure expressing inability is replaced by 'so...that + subject + cannot + verb'.

parts.statement: doctor / apple / all / day / keeps / a / away / the (Rearrange the words to make a meaningful sentence)
parts.explanation:
Meaningful Sentence: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

Explanation:
Rearranging the jumbled words produces the standard English proverb.

parts.statement: The man is a doctor. He is wearing a blue sweater. (Combine the pair of sentences using 'who')
parts.explanation:
Combined Sentence: The man who is wearing a blue sweater is a doctor.

Explanation:
The relative pronoun 'who' is used to join the two sentences by substituting the pronoun 'He'.

parts.statement: To save animals is our moral duty. (Rewrite the sentence beginning with 'It')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: It is our moral duty to save animals.

Explanation:
The sentence is restructured using the dummy/preparatory subject 'It' at the beginning.

parts.statement: If you do not tell the truth, you will be punished. (Use 'unless' in place of 'if')
parts.explanation:
Rewritten Sentence: Unless you tell the truth, you will be punished.

Explanation:
'Unless' means 'if not', so 'If...do not' is replaced directly by 'Unless' while making the clause affirmative.

parts.statement: He cut his finger with knife. (Change into simple present tense)
parts.explanation:
Simple Present Sentence: He cuts his finger with a knife.

Explanation:
In the simple present tense with a third-person singular subject ('He'), the verb takes the '-s' suffix ('cuts').

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 30 words: (any six)

parts.statement: What does courage mean to Mandela?
parts.explanation: To Nelson Mandela, courage does not mean the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. He believes that a brave man is not one who does not feel afraid, but one who conquers that fear.

parts.statement: What was Valli's favourite pastime?
parts.explanation: Valli's favourite pastime was standing in the front doorway of her house and watching the street outside, especially watching the bus that traveled between her village and the town.

parts.statement: Why does the postmaster send money to Lencho?
parts.explanation: The postmaster was deeply impressed by Lencho's firm and unshakable faith in God. He collected money from his employees and friends to send to Lencho so that Lencho's faith in God would not be shaken.

parts.statement: What 'experiment' did Maxwell think Camusfearna would be suitable for?
parts.explanation: Gavin Maxwell thought that Camusfearna, being surrounded by water near the coast, would be a suitable place for an experiment in keeping an otter as a pet instead of a dog.

parts.statement: Why was Mr. Keesing annoyed with Anne?
parts.explanation: Mr. Keesing, the maths teacher, was annoyed with Anne Frank because she talked excessively during his classes, disrupting the lessons despite several verbal warnings.

parts.statement: "I'll take the risk". What is the risk? Why does the narrator take it?
parts.explanation: The risk was flying his old Dakota airplane straight into the huge, dark storm clouds over Paris. The narrator took the risk because he was eager to get home and have a traditional English breakfast with his family.

parts.statement: What does Kisa Gotami ask for? Does she get it?
parts.explanation: Grief-stricken Kisa Gotami asks for medicine to bring her dead son back to life. She does not get it because death is inevitable and no medicine can restore life to the deceased.

parts.statement: What are the elders in Goa nostalgic about?
parts.explanation: The elders in Goa are nostalgic about the good old Portuguese days, the Portuguese people, and their famous, traditional loaves of bread prepared by traditional village bakers.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 30 words: (any two)

parts.statement: How did Griffin, the scientist become invisible?
parts.explanation: Griffin carried out experiments and swallowed certain rare drugs that made his body transparent like a sheet of glass, rendering him completely invisible to the human eye.

parts.statement: What does Horace Danby like to collect?
parts.explanation: Horace Danby loves collecting rare and expensive books. To fulfill his passion, he robbed one safe every year to buy the books he desired through an agent.

parts.statement: Why is Mrs. Pumphrey worried about Tricki?
parts.explanation: Mrs. Pumphrey was worried because her pet dog Tricki became listless, lost all energy, refused to eat his favourite dishes, and suffered from repeated bouts of vomiting.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 30 words: (any two)

parts.statement: How does the poet suggest that you identify the Asian lion? (How to Tell Wild Animals)
parts.explanation: The poet suggests that if you travel to the jungles of the East and encounter a large, tawny-colored beast that roars fiercely as you are dying, it is the Asian Lion.

parts.statement: What does the poet compare the branches of the tree to? (The Trees)
parts.explanation: In the poem 'The Trees', the poet compares the long-cramped branches of the trees to newly discharged hospital patients who move toward the clinic doors feeling dazed and confused.

parts.statement: What could Amanda do if she were a mermaid? (Amanda)
parts.explanation: If Amanda were a mermaid, she would drift blissfully alone on the calm, emerald sea, enjoying complete freedom away from her mother's constant nagging.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 75 words: (any one)

parts.statement: How did Mandela's understanding of freedom change with age and experience?
parts.explanation: As a young boy, Nelson Mandela understood freedom in a personal, physical sense—being free to run in the fields, swim in the stream, and stay out at night. As a university student, he viewed freedom as the ability to stay out late and read what he pleased. However, with age and experience, he realized that his boyhood freedom was an illusion. His perspective broadened to understand that freedom meant the dignity and equality of all Black South Africans suffering under apartheid, prompting him to join the African National Congress.

parts.statement: How did Valli save up money for her first journey? Was it easy for her?
parts.explanation: Valli saved up money for her first bus journey by meticulously hoarding every stray coin that came her way. She firmly suppressed childish temptations to buy peppermints, toys, balloons, and rides on the merry-go-round at the village fair. Saving sixty paise was not easy for an eight-year-old child, but her intense desire to ride the bus gave her the self-control and determination needed to achieve her goal.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 75 words: (any one)

parts.statement: Write the central idea of the poem 'The Ball Poem'.
parts.explanation: The central idea of 'The Ball Poem' by John Berryman revolves around accepting loss as an inevitable part of human life. The loss of the boy's ball symbolizes the loss of innocent childhood days. The poet emphasizes that material possessions can be replaced, but lost memories and time cannot. The poem highlights the importance of developing resilience, coping with grief, and learning to stand up and move forward in a world of possessions.

parts.statement: What colour is the young woman's hair? What does she say she can change it to?
parts.explanation: The young woman's hair is honey-colored (yellow/golden). She states that she can dye her hair brown, black, or carrot color. She wants to change her hair color to demonstrate that men should love her for her true internal self—her character and soul—rather than being attracted merely to her superficial physical appearance or external beauty.

questions.text: Answer the following questions in about 75 words: (any one)

parts.statement: What are the qualities that go into the making of a scientist?
parts.explanation: According to the lesson 'The Making of a Scientist', three essential qualities are required to become a scientist: a first-rate mind, sharp curiosity, and the determination to win for the right reasons. Richard Ebright possessed these traits from an early age. His inquisitive nature, encouraged by his mother, led him to collect butterflies, conduct meticulous experiments, and persevere through failures to make groundbreaking contributions to molecular biology.

parts.statement: How did Bholi's teacher play an important role in changing the course of her life?
parts.explanation: Bholi's teacher played a pivotal role in transforming her life. When Bholi first joined school, she was an insecure, stammering girl who felt inferior due to her pockmarked face. The teacher treated her with immense warmth, affection, and patience. She inspired Bholi with confidence, taught her to speak without stammering, and educated her. This education empowered Bholi to evolve into an independent woman who boldly rejected a greedy groom, choosing instead to serve her parents and teach at the school.
